GSA uses the Do Not Pay System prior to payment disbursement as part of its ongoing efforts to prevent improper payments. Treasury screens each of GSA's Payment Automation Manager (PAM) files against certain sources in the Do Not Pay system when submitted, and returns matches with indicators of risk. Most matches for salary payments are timing related due to recently deceased employees who did not have their HR action processed before the payroll cycle was disbursed. In addition, GSA’s financial management system vendors are submitted to the Do Not Pay portal each month. Any matches are researched to verify that the vendor has been marked "Debarred" or "Inactive" to prevent future payments. These processes along with others reduce the risk of improper payments for over $27 billion dollars of GSA payments in FY 2026. In FY 2026, twelve payments for $78,000 were returned by Do Not Pay.


In FY 2025 and FY 2026, GSA completed new Do Not Pay onboarding requirements as outlined in Executive Order (EO) 14249 (Protecting America’s Bank Account Against Fraud, Waste, and Abuse) and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-25-32. GSA documented programs and payment types, updated data access agreements and system of records notices (SORNs) for Privacy Act-related data, completed an analysis of matching program requirements, and worked with the Do Not Pay team to identify user and data exchange requirements. The Do Not Pay initiative continues to help reduce improper payments at GSA.

VA utilizes various methods to identify and recover overpayments. At VA, these audits are performed in two major areas: Veterans Health Administration for three programs providing health care and Supply Fund payments in the Office of Revolving Fund. These are discussed in more detail below. 

Veterans Health Administration 
The Veterans Health Administration utilizes a recovery audit contract, which will audit claims for three programs: Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs, Purchased Long Term Services and Supports, and VA Community Care. Payments were tested to ensure the reimbursement was based on the appropriate methodology and that the medical records support the diagnostic related group billed for the services. 

During FY 2026, the recovery audit identified overpayments where the medical record did not substantiate the services billed or the coding was not accurate based on a review of documents. Solutions to resolve these conditions are being developed but will not be implemented until FY 2027. The identified overpayments resulted in re-adjudication of the original payments in the claims processing system, leading to bills of collections being issued to the community care providers. Additional methods used to recover overpayments include internal off-sets and Treasury’s Invoice Payment Processing Payment off-set.

Office of Revolving Funds 
The Office of Revolving Funds collaborates with the VA Office of Inspector General to perform recovery audits on VA's Supply Fund program. Overpayments identified are mostly due to non-compliance with contract billing requirements on federal supply schedule contracts. These conditions are being resolved by education provided by the VA Office of Inspector General to non-conforming vendors. The VA Office of Inspector General identifies an overpayment, and a bill of collection is then prepared by the Office of Revolving Funds with appropriate terms of collection. If the vendor chooses to dispute the bill of collection VA will work towards appropriate resolution.

The Department of State's Bureau of the Comptroller and Global Financial Services (CGFS) provides financial management services to the Department and other agencies. CGFS monitors improper payments through a two-tiered review process. First, payment-issuing offices review every payment before disbursement. Second, CGFS’ Office of Governance and Oversight (CGFS/GOV) conducts internal post-payment audits, using random and targeted samples of domestic, overseas, and employee payments. 

Domestic vendor payments make up the largest category of Department payments subject to Payment Integrity Information Act (PIIA) recovery audit requirements. Each month, CGFS/GOV runs an automated comparison of vendor invoice data against prior-year payments and flags potential duplicates for recapture audit analysis. This automated process has proven a cost-effective way to review domestic payments. Each quarter, CGFS/GOV also manually reviews samples of domestic and overseas payments. It reviews supporting documentation to confirm that the Department paid the correct vendor the correct amount. 

CGFS/GOV also audits employee payments each quarter, including permanent change of station (PCS) travel, temporary duty (TDY) travel, tuition and education allowances, representation expenses, local transportation, and other reimbursements. These audits review supporting documentation to confirm that payments are accurate and comply with regulations. 

Historically, the most common causes of potential improper payments were caused by insufficient supporting documentation or a misinterpretation of applicable regulations. Generally, only minimal amounts have been referred for recapture because of recovery audits. In FY 2026, the Department of State identified $0 in improper payments through recovery audits. 

CGFS continues to review these processes and, where possible, uses automation and super intelligence (SI) tools to make them more efficient and effective.

The Department of State (the Department) uses the Department of the Treasury's Do Not Pay (DNP) Working System to prevent and detect improper payments before and after disbursement. DNP has reduced improper payments at the Department. 

In FY 2026, Treasury’s Payment Verification replaced the legacy Payment Integration that was previously in the Do Not Pay Web Portal. As part of the Payment Verification, agencies are no longer required to adjudicate death matches in the DNP portal. Instead, the Payments module in the Do Not Pay Web Portal was redesigned with the Treasury’s Bureau of the Fiscal Service (BFS) Payment Verification (PV) screening initiative, allowing users to easily interpret and view PV screening results. The Department is utilizing this new DNP Web Portal for online searches and the legacy system for other screenings. Death Screening went online in January. Treasury granted the Department an extension until December 31, 2026, to implement Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) payment verification. 

In FY 2026, the Department soft launched Death Screening, verifying 1,061,997 payments totaling $11.66 billion, with 21 returned payments totaling $109,518. The Department performed 869 DNP Web Portal online searches, as needed, and on a daily and monthly basis screened 50,511,204 records with 43,558 match results through the Legacy system. 

At least twice each month, the Department screens its annuitant database against the Death Master File (DMF) to identify deceased annuitants. The Department researches every match and, once it confirms a match, stops the disbursement before the monthly annuity payment is processed. In FY 2026, the Department screened 216,782 annuitant payments, totaling $1.3 billion, and stopped 534 payments, totaling $2.8 million. The Department also checks every manual annuity payment processed through Treasury's Secure Payment System against the DMF before it releases payment. 

For overseas payments issued by non-Treasury disbursing offices, the Department screens payee information against the Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list. In FY 2026, the Department screened 2,215,171 payments, totaling $7.9 billion. None of these payments required a stop. 

The Department processes grant payments through the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Payment Management System (PMS). HHS uses the DNP portal to identify recipients who owe delinquent federal non-tax debt, are listed as deceased on the DMF, or are excluded from doing business with the federal government. In FY 2026, HHS found no ineligible Department grant recipients. In FY 2026, the Treasury Offset Program (TOP) stopped one recipient payment. TOP is administered by Treasury's Bureau of Fiscal Service. It collects delinquent debts owed to federal agencies and states, including past-due child support, under 26 U.S.C. 6402(d), 31 U.S.C. 3720A, and other applicable laws.

The Small Business Administration (SBA) has integrated Treasury’s Do Not Pay (DNP) Initiative into its payment integrity and pre-award screening workflows. Programmatic loan disbursements are systematically validated against DNP both pre-award and pre-loan disbursement. For SBA’s grant programs, Grant Solutions Recipient Data Insights, an integrated DNP capability within Grant Solutions, is used. 
 
1. DNP Databases & Verification Sources Used 
To ensure comprehensive screening across death records, exclusions, sanctions, and credit risks, the SBA leverages daily API connectivity to query key federal DNP databases, including: 
•	Department of Defense Death Source (DOD) 
•	Department of State Death Source (DOS) 
•	Death Master File (DMF) 
•	Obituary Death Source (AIS-OBIT) 
•	Probate Death Source (AIS-PROB) 
•	System for Award Management (SAM) Entity Registration 
•	List of Excluded Individuals/Entities (LEIE-PUB) – Screening individuals and entities excluded from participating in Medicare, Medicaid, and other federal healthcare programs. 
•	Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) – Identifying blocked assets and sanctioned entities/persons prohibited from conducting business with U.S. parties. 
•	Credit Alert Verification Reporting System (CAIVRS) – Credit alert and delinquent federal debt screening. 
•	Treasury Offset Program (TOP) – Debt check screening. 
  
2. Frequency of Review & System Automation 
Pre-award and pre-disbursement checks are automated via daily API calls integrated directly into agency financial management systems, enabling real-time verification. During Fiscal Year 2026, the SBA executed 2,146,970 DNP API calls to maintain continuous system-to-system verification. 
   
3. Scope of FY 2026 Payments Reviewed 
During Fiscal Year 2026, the SBA reviewed over 17,000 pre-disbursement transactions, totaling more than $1.133 billion in program outlays.  
 
4. Improper Payments Prevented & Corrective Actions 
Through rigorous pre-award screening, DNP checks served as an effective front-end control by stopping 7,472 applications from becoming loans during FY 2026.  
•	Pre-Disbursement Controls: When DNP match anomalies are flagged prior to disbursement, the SBA requires the intended recipient to successfully resolve the finding before becoming eligible for SBA funding. 
•	Post-Disbursement Remediation: For anomalies identified on disbursements already released, the SBA immediately places a hold code on the loan or grant and/or denies future financial assistance, loan relief, or awards until the recipient fully resolves the DNP finding.
